findings.priority_reason: Before claiming2–3s usable delivery or relying on the affected boundary.
findings.title: Fresh generation cannot meet the2–3s budget
findings.root_cause: Full document and code resources are regenerated inline, followed by semantic review.
findings.condition: A new task goes through the measured normal four-call path.
findings.consequence: Mean58.74s, body alone47.57s, zero of three ready under3s.
findings.counterevidence: Exact-task cached delivery already runs without a model locally; the entire codebase is not intrinsically slow.
findings.fix: Separate prepared approved Skill retrieval/task binding from offline compilation; if arbitrary new long-form generation must also finish in3s, treat that capability as unproven until output/model/quality measurements establish it.
findings.verification: Freeze new tasks, measure request-to-usable-ready latency and failures including cache misses, source checks and any selection model.

impacts.reason: The primary architecture does not fit the explicit interactive deadline.
Necessary latency capability fails in the observed normal workload.

findings.priority_reason: Before claiming2–3s usable delivery or relying on the affected boundary.
findings.title: Final reply duplication prevents usable delivery
findings.root_cause: The transport attaches a whole Build and repeats its rendered main/references in skill.
findings.condition: Approved new task body fits independently but the final compound JSON exceeds32768 bytes.
findings.consequence: Normal delivery fails2/3 despite correct guard behavior and complete stored bodies.
findings.counterevidence: The byte guard is correct and the approved internal build is retained; bypassing it or raising the cap is not the validated fix.
findings.fix: Add an explicit small public-delivery contract with artifact identity/bundle and minimal binding; retain internal build/audit via authorized separate lookup and preserve legacy calls.
findings.verification: All frozen bodies deliver through the new public path within the unchanged cap; unauthorized/stale/tampered/partial bundles still fail.

impacts.reason: Ordinary output saturation has no usable bounded primary result.
High body scores do not complete the primary consumption interaction.

findings.priority_reason: Before the next low-latency pilot; use the existing shared mechanisms.
findings.title: Exact task cache is not a reusable published Skill resolver
findings.root_cause: Task context is stored with the generated document; cache identity includes literal goal and environment/limits. The demo registry is empty and storage is ephemeral.
findings.condition: The caller asks the same job using different wording or starts a new example host.
findings.consequence: The existing fast exact-identity path is not reached; an ordinary paraphrase becomes pending generation.
findings.counterevidence: Exact identity caching works and correctly partitions authority; deleting goal or principal from its key would be unsafe.
findings.fix: Keep the exact cache key safe; add stable approved Skill identities with task bindings and LLM applicability selection via existing Registry/authority/source ports.
findings.verification: Paraphrases select a suitable approved Skill with provenance and no new document generation; unrelated/scope-incompatible requests do not auto-hit by similarity.

impacts.reason: Cross-request reuse needed for low-latency interaction is not established.

findings.priority_reason: Before the next low-latency pilot; use the existing shared mechanisms.
findings.title: Content grading is insufficient as the adoption gate
findings.root_cause: Model judges can attribute source instructions to generated content and body scores omit delivery/time success.
findings.condition: A judge sees source guidance and a superficially complete generated plan.
findings.consequence: The keyboard document is graded as explicitly using key although it omits that condition.
findings.counterevidence: Fixed tests and passage-ID validation detect structural violations; the current report already retains explicit corrections instead of hiding them.
findings.fix: Retain source-linked adjudication and add hard ready-within-budget/delivery/negative-boundary gates, with blinded non-development tasks.
findings.verification: Unsupported criterion claims are caught, pending/failure never count as fast-ready success, and corrected scores remain distinct from raw judgments.

impacts.reason: Existing synthetic contract tests are useful, but semantic grade evidence still requires direct validation.

findings.priority_reason: Before the next low-latency pilot; use the existing shared mechanisms.
findings.title: Query rewriting remains a separate language-triggered step
findings.root_cause: The example auto mode uses script/title heuristics to add another inference before retrieval.
findings.condition: A Japanese/non-title query follows the measured adapter.
findings.consequence: About1.34s mean is spent rewriting; disabling it blindly may harm retrieval and still leaves the47.57s body call.
findings.counterevidence: This is only~2.3% of observed wall time, and rewrite can improve English-index retrieval. It is not the root fix.
findings.fix: Let the calling LLM supply the authorized public query or pre-index multilingual metadata; validate retrieval quality and avoid keyword-specific routing.
findings.verification: Held-out multilingual/paraphrased queries retain retrieval/selection quality; no hidden/internal context is sent to external search.
